source.title: Circuit Component Reuse Across Tasks in Transformer Language Models
source.authors: Jack Merullo; Carsten Eickhoff; Ellie Pavlick

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The authors explicitly reproduce the IOI circuit on GPT2-Medium using path patching closely following Wang et al. (2022), and report circuit findings on that model.
record.gate_note: The study also path-patches GPT2-Medium on Colored Objects and other tasks, and reports interventions on the Colored Objects circuit. It does not test backup-head self-repair, compare circuit-finding methods, or test IOI across the prompt variants specified in V6. The GPT2-Large and GPT2-XL results are preliminary head-to-logit analyses.
record.test_reason: The study reruns Wang et al.'s path-patching procedure for IOI on GPT2-Medium. It reports that the same component classes reappear there, then measures how far those components are reused for Colored Objects, Greater Than and World Capitals, and in GPT2-Large and GPT2-XL. All of these are V3 questions: the same circuit in other sizes and tasks. The study never analyses GPT-2 small itself, so its results do not bear on V1 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but it leaves out three things. The authors also claim to reproduce the IOI circuit on GPT2-Medium, with a negative mover head that demotes S2. They frame reuse as an inhibition-mover subcircuit for selecting among alternatives in context. They note that, in the preliminary analysis, exact-head overlap falls as model size grows, while mover roles persist.
record.recipe_differences: The authors follow Wang et al. (2022) path patching closely for IOI, but use GPT2-Medium rather than GPT-2 small and also analyze a modified Colored Objects task. They allow MLPs to be recomputed. Their overlap calculation uses a top-2% threshold and they explicitly note that overlap is difficult to quantify.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported IOI/Colored Objects head overlap depends on the top-2% importance threshold. On Colored Objects, the correct option's position affects the observed attention redistribution when content-gatherer attention is blocked. The authors also report that top-head overlap differs between GPT2-Large and GPT2-XL.

fits_no_version.finding: On Colored Objects, mover-head attention redistribution after blocking obj2 depends on the position of the correct colour. Head 19.15 also over-promotes 'brown'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT2-Medium's copying heads on list-selection tasks have position and token biases unrelated to IOI circuit structure.

record.problems: The study's main circuit-overlap estimate uses a chosen top-2% threshold, and the authors say there is no exact solution for quantifying overlap. GPT2-Large and GPT2-XL analyses are preliminary and compare top 10 heads. The modified Colored Objects task is reported as 1000 examples, but the paper gives both 49.6% and 49.7% as baseline accuracy. The intervention results intentionally set attention patterns and are on Colored Objects rather than IOI.

untested.parts: The circuit in GPT-2 small itself, the 26-head/7-class count, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. The study works only on GPT2-Medium and larger.
Backup name-mover heads and self-repair under ablation; not examined.
Training checkpoints. The full IOI circuit (beyond the head-to-logit mover stage) in GPT2-Large and GPT2-XL. Models outside the GPT-2 family.
Alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types and metrics. Only path patching is used.
Faithfulness and completeness under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
IOI name orders, templates and numbers of names.

missing.what: Without intervention, the IOI inhibition heads hurt slightly on Colored Objects: patching them improves logit difference by about 1-3%. The negative mover 19.1 contributes only about 1% of logit difference, against being the most important head in IOI.
Per-head logit-difference contributions of the mover heads in Colored Objects (15.14 about 28%, 16.15 about 13%), and their relative importance in IOI (18.5 most important there).
Zero-ablating the content-gatherer heads drops accuracy to about chance, similar to blocking attention to obj2.

record.verdict_notes: Merullo et al. is not an original source, so verdicts are allowed. r1 and r2 move from V1 to V3 because the model is GPT2-Medium. The intervention accuracy rows (r8-r10) induce behaviour on purpose and are unlinked; r11 and r12 are kept because they test whether the downstream circuit interactions are reused. The paper names the third inhibition head inconsistently (13.14 vs 13.13). r13 lists the wrong overlapping head: 20.14 should be 21.8.

versions.untested_parts: Tests the IOI circuit on GPT2-Medium, not GPT-2 small. Does not establish the original circuit's 26-head/seven-class count or explicitly evaluate faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads to test self-repair or backup heads.

Tests IOI and Colored Objects on GPT2-Medium, with preliminary IOI/Colored Objects head comparisons on GPT2-Large and GPT2-XL, and also reports circuit overlap for other tasks. Does not test other training checkpoints or establish broad reuse across models beyond those reported.
Uses path patching; does not compare alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics for recovering the same circuit.
Does not systematically compare IOI circuit faithfulness or completeness across ablation types, metrics, or prompt distributions.
Does not test IOI across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.measure: Whether the IO token is preferred to the subject token in the logits
rows.note: The authors say the analyzed models perform well on this task.
rows.check: This is a capability check: the IO token is preferred to the subject 100% of the time. It says nothing about which components carry the behaviour, so it should not support any version.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched attention-head paths to logits, mover-head queries, and inhibition-head values
rows.measure: Identified component roles and circuit structure
rows.value: The authors report active duplicate-token/induction, inhibition, mover, and negative-mover components; the named inhibition heads are 12.3, 13.4, and 13.14, and negative mover head 19.1 attends to S2 and demotes it.
rows.note: The paper describes this as reproducing the IOI circuit on the larger model, with differences from GPT2-Small, including the negative mover's behavior.
rows.check: Relink from V1 to V3: the model is GPT2-Medium, not GPT-2 small. Duplicate/induction, inhibition and mover heads all reappear. The negative mover head 19.1 behaves differently: it attends only to S2 and is the most important head. The paper names the third inhibition head 13.14 in Fig. 6 and C.3 but 13.13 in Sections 5 and D.3. No head count and no faithfulness, completeness or minimality test is reported.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Compared the most important heads in the path-patched IOI and Colored Objects circuits

conditions.value: Top 2% most important heads for each circuit

rows.note: The authors describe the difference as three inhibition heads and one negative mover head being replaced by three content gatherer heads. They caution that circuit overlap is difficult to quantify.
rows.check: The 25/32 (78%) overlap depends on the authors' top-2% threshold, which they acknowledge (Appendix I.3).

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched heads to logits and mover-head queries and values
rows.measure: Reported component roles and overlap with IOI
rows.value: The authors identify shared mover heads, including 15.14 and 16.15, and duplicate-token/induction heads; content gatherer heads 11.6, 11.7, and 12.15 take a role they contrast with IOI inhibition heads.
rows.note: The analysis is on Colored Objects, not another IOI prompt format.
rows.check: Mover and induction/duplicate heads are shared. The inhibition step, however, is replaced by content-gatherer heads, and the negative mover contributes only about 1% of logit difference. So reuse covers only part of the IOI circuit.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated unmodified model on the Colored Objects task
rows.note: The paper gives both 49.6% and 49.7% as the pre-intervention accuracy.
rows.check: Baseline accuracy on Colored Objects is a performance value, not a circuit measure. The paper reports both 49.6% and 49.7%.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Blocked content gatherer attention from the final position to the question information

conditions.value: Question information hypothesized to be passed by content gatherers

rows.baseline: 49.6% on the unmodified task (reported in Figure 5)
rows.note: The authors describe this as roughly chance-level selection among the three test-example colors.
rows.check: This tests the role of content-gatherer heads, which are specific to Colored Objects and are not IOI components. It bears on no version.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Applied the same attention-blocking intervention using randomly selected heads not predicted to perform content gathering

conditions.value: Three randomly sampled heads from the relevant layers; three seeds

rows.note: Random-head blocking did not produce the accuracy drop reported for blocking the hypothesized content-gatherer signal.
rows.check: This is the random-head control for r6. It is not a test of any version.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium

rows.note: The intervention intentionally sets the head's attention pattern.
rows.check: Accuracy after forcing the negative mover head's attention is an induced intervention. It does not show the component being reused unprompted.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on three inhibition heads' attention patterns to direct them to incorrect color options
rows.uncertainty: Error bars shown as standard error in Figure 5; numeric value not stated
rows.note: The intervention intentionally sets the heads' attention patterns.
rows.check: Induced attention-pattern intervention on the inhibition heads; accuracy is not a measure of natural reuse. Heads are listed as 12.3, 13.4, 13.13.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on three inhibition heads and the negative mover head's attention patterns to direct them to incorrect color options

conditions.value: Inhibition heads 12.3, 13.4, 13.13 and negative mover head 19.1

rows.baseline: 49.7% in the intervention section; Figure 5 gives 49.6%
rows.uncertainty: Error bars shown as standard error in Figure 5; numeric value not stated
rows.note: The authors state that the intervention introduced zero new mistakes.
rows.check: Induced intervention on both the inhibition and negative mover heads. The rise from 49.7% to 93.7% shows that forcing these heads helps, not that they are reused unprompted.

rows.subject: GPT2-Medium
rows.operation_detail: Compared mover-head attention to incorrect colors before and after the inhibition-head intervention

conditions.value: The 496 examples the unmodified model originally gets right

rows.uncertainty: Error bars shown as standard error; numeric value not stated
rows.note: The paper reports that attention to the correct color remained high or increased.
rows.check: This happens under intervention, but it measures whether downstream mover heads respond to inhibition-head input as in IOI. That bears on whether the inhibition-mover subcircuit is reused.

relationships.reason: Path patching recovers duplicate/induction, inhibition and mover heads in GPT2-Medium, as in GPT-2 small (r2). The negative mover role differs: it demotes S2 only.
relationships.display_finding: Path patching recovers duplicate-token, induction, inhibition and mover heads, although the negative mover demotes only S2.

source_check.reason: Section 3 and Appendix C recover duplicate/induction, inhibition and mover components; the negative mover specifically demotes S2.

relationships.condition: GPT2-Medium, IOI components reused for Colored Objects (mover/induction heads and the inhibition-mover interaction)
relationships.reason: 25/32 top-2% heads are shared, and the same mover and induction heads carry Colored Objects (r3, r4). Forcing inhibition makes mover heads attend less to wrong colours (-8.7%) and roughly triples their logit attribution, as the IOI circuit predicts (r11, r12).
relationships.display_finding: The tasks share 25/32 heads ranked in the top 2%; forcing inhibition reduces mover attention to wrong colours by 8.7% and roughly triples logit attribution.

relationships.reason: Content-gatherer heads replace the inhibition step. The inhibition heads give a noisy signal that slightly hurts, and the negative mover contributes about 1% (r4). Based on the text of Sections 4.4 and D.1, which no row records; see missing.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report IOI performance and describe a path-patched circuit with duplicate/induction, inhibition, mover, and negative-mover roles, consistent with reproducing the circuit on this model (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Targeted interventions on the proposed inhibition and negative-mover components substantially improve Colored Objects accuracy, but this is an induced intervention result on a different task, not evidence that all behavior is carried by the unmodified IOI circuit (r5, r8, r9, r10).
